title: Hang a small tool shelf on the French cleat along a workbench's backboard
instruction: Hang the shelf on the cleat rail so it sits flat against the backboard and level, and let go.
context: French cleats are a common way to hang heavy things at home: kitchen wall cabinets, bathroom mirrors, and the tool walls of home garages and workshops, where shelves, bins and tool holders hang on one long cleat and are moved around at will. One strip, its top edge cut at 45 degrees, is screwed to the wall or to a workbench's back upstand (backboard); its twin is screwed to the back of the unit. Anyone who has hung one knows the move: lift the unit clear of the wall strip, set it back until its strip meets the board, and lower it so the bevels mate and draw it in. A unit lowered short of the board comes down in front of the strip, one lowered skewed hangs from one end, one slid sideways overhangs the strip's end, and none of these holds a load. Here a small tool shelf starts on the bench and is done when it hangs flat to the board, level, on its whole strip, with nobody holding it.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is z = 0; x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up; arm bases at y +30.5 cm and -30.5 cm. (1) The bench's back upstand (backboard), fixed: a cream-painted plywood board 30 mm thick (x 400 to 430 mm), 700 mm wide (y -350 to +350 mm), 210 mm tall, front face at x 400 mm, held upright by two fixed pine braces behind it screwed to the bench top (40 mm wide, 30 mm tall, x 430 to 560 mm, at y -250 and +250 mm). (2) The bench's end post, fixed pine, 30 x 30 mm, 210 mm tall, against the backboard on the robot's left: x 370 to 400 mm, y 270 to 300 mm. (3) A fixed cleat rail (the board's cleat), birch plywood, 11 mm thick (x 389 to 400 mm), 340 mm long (y -170 to +170 mm), bottom edge at z 20 mm; its top edge is cut at 45 degrees and descends toward the board: z 61 mm at its front face and z 50 mm at the board. Three grey 8 mm pan-head screws hold it to the backboard (y -120, 0 and +120 mm, z 30 mm, heads 1.5 mm proud). (4) A loose tool shelf, birch plywood, 0.53 kg, one rigid body, open at the top and front: 320 mm wide (y), 100 mm deep (x), 80 mm tall; two end panels 18 mm thick, a bottom 6 mm and a back 6 mm thick between them; the matching cleat screwed to its back: birch plywood 12 mm thick (x), 300 mm long (y, centred), top edge 70 mm over the shelf's underside, lower edge cut at 45 degrees, 22 mm over the underside at its front face and 10 mm at its back face; three 8 mm pan-head screws through the back panel hold it (heads inside, y -100, 0 and +100 mm, 50 mm up). (5) The shelf starts standing on the table on its underside, centred on y 0, box at x 170 to 270 mm, unit cleat at x 270 to 282 mm, its cleat toward the backboard. Hung, the unit cleat's back face is on the backboard (x 400 mm), the box's back face at x 388 mm, the underside 40 mm over the table and the two bevels face to face. To go on or come off, the shelf must be lifted about 11 mm above its seat, its underside to about 51 mm: its cleat's lowest edge, 10 mm over the underside, has to pass over the rail's 61 mm front edge (the eased corners take a little off). Carried 14 mm short of the backboard it is lowered in front of the cleat. Nothing else is on the table. All sizes are design values for the build in the README (a cut list), not a commercial product.
scoring: End state, read at the last step from the pose of the shelf and from both grippers (the backboard is fixed). The unit cleat's two ends are projected on the backboard; the part of it over the cleat rail (y -170 to +170 mm) is the engaged length, 0 to 300 mm, between points A and B. Bevel contact at A (or B): the unit cleat's bevel face lies on the cleat rail's bevel plane within 1 mm at two points 10 mm apart along the slope, and the two faces overlap by 4 mm or more along the slope. Seated: at A and B the unit cleat's back face is from 1.5 mm off the backboard to 1 mm into it and the shelf's underside is 38 to 42 mm over the table; level: its long axis within 1 degree of horizontal; plumb: its back face within 1 degree of vertical. Hands off: on every step of the last 1 s both grippers' finger zones are 30 mm or more from the shelf, and over that 1 s it moves under 1 mm and turns under 0.3 degrees. Score 0 unless hands off. Otherwise: 1.0 bevel contact at A and B, all 300 mm engaged (the unit cleat's ends within the rail's ends), seated, level and plumb; 0.5 bevel contact at A and B, 150 mm or more engaged, back face no more than 8 mm off the backboard (or 3 mm into it), level and plumb within 3 degrees (hung but not fully mated, offset along the board or slightly crooked); 0.25 bevel contact at one of A, B only (hung from one end), or at both with the shelf outside the 0.5 limits; 0 otherwise (on the table, in front of the cleat, resting on the cleat's edge, leaning, upside down). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Success: 1.0 held for 1 s. In a real trial, per condition: bevel contact, a 1 mm feeler will not enter between the faces within 40 mm of A or B; seated, a 1.5 mm feeler between back face and backboard at A and B and a rule from the table to the underside (38 to 42 mm); engaged length, a rule along the cleats' ends; level, a torpedo level on the shelf's bottom; plumb, a try square on its back; hands off, a 30 mm spacer block against each hand and 30 fps video of the last 1 s; still, a dial indicator (0.01 mm) on a magnetic base touching the top of each end panel, read over the last 1 s: each changes under 0.8 mm (0.3 degrees of turn is 0.8 mm at the panels, 151 mm from the centre, so this also keeps movement under 1 mm).
fidelity: Rigid bodies; plywood as solid boxes (680 kg/m3, est), friction 0.45 ply on ply (est). The two 45 degree faces are 2.5 mm slabs with arrises eased 2 mm, so the faces meet over 7 mm of run. Screws: heads only, cleats fixed to their parts. The backboard is a 210 mm bench upstand: the arms' wrists pass over its top edge, so a full-height wall would not leave them room. The shelf is a small tool ledge, 0.53 kg. Sizes are design values (README cut list), not measured off a bought part.
reset_notes: The backboard (screwed to its braces and the bench), braces, end post and cleat rail stay fixed (check the rail's bevel is clean and its top edge is 50 mm over the table at the board). Stand the shelf on the table on its underside, centred on y 0, box at x 170 to 270 mm, unit cleat toward the backboard (at x 270 to 282 mm), end panels square to the board. Nothing is consumed; wipe any dust off both bevels.
